title: SummitCore Implementation Kickoff - Staging & SLA Review
next_steps: Send staging runbook and network checklist
Share SLA one-pager and uptime targets
Provide security pack (SOC2 certs, audit logs)
action_items: Maya Patel: Share staging runbook and sample infra diagram by 2026-04-09
Liam O'Connor: Prepare benchmark harness and perf test plan by 2026-04-12
Karen Lee (SummitCore): Provision VPC peering and provide CIDR by 2026-04-10
Priya Nair (SummitCore): Send required compliance checklist and current SOC2 scope by 2026-04-11
header: Date: 2026-04-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Location: Zoom | Recording: Yes
summary: Kickoff for SummitCore's implementation with Redwood. Reviewed staging connectivity, initial SLA targets, pilot scope and success metrics. Identified networking and compliance action items; agreed to pilot benchmark next week.
transcript:
00:00 - Maya Patel: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and we wanted to run through staging, sla expectations, and next steps. can folks introduce quickly?
00:12 - Aisha Khan: yeah hi I'm Aisha head of ml at SummitCore, we own model infra and inference.
00:18 - Roberto Diaz: Roberto, VP Eng, i'll be sponsor for infra and cost decisions.
:24 - Karen Lee: Karen, devops, i'll set up networking.
00:27 - Liam O'Connor: Liam, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll be helping with benchmarks.
00:32 - Sofia Reyes: Sofia, CSM, helping onboarding and timelines.
00:36 - Maya: great, thanks. quick agenda: staging network and peering, sla targets, pilot workload we want to run, security artifacts. then wrap with next steps.
01:02 - Aisha: to give a bit of context, our use case is customer-facing summarization and a reranking microservice. p99 latency target is around 300-350ms for 512 tokens on peak periods. cost is also big — we have a $X per 1,000 token target, so need tradeoffs.
01:28 - Roberto: yeah we want to avoid overprovisioning; we'll consider dedicated or hosted depending on throughput. initial pilot should prove economics.
01:40 - Liam: great makes sense — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private VPC. for pilot we usually start with a dedicated small pool in staging to reproduce production traffic, and then show cost/latency.
02:05 - Karen: on networking, we prefer VPC peering; can you outline what you need? firewall rules etc.
02:12 - Maya: sure. we have two options: 1) temporary public endpoint with IP allowlist for staging; or 2) VPC peering for private deployment. peering is preferred for security. we need CIDR, regions, and a service account for the peering setup.
02:38 - Karen: we can do peering, we'll need a diagram and clear runbook.
02:45 - Maya: we'll send a staging runbook with steps and required info.
02:49 - Liam: also worth noting some customers use an on-prem connector; if you plan on air-gapped or HSM, that's a follow-on.
03:05 - Aisha: we're not air-gapped, but we do require KMS integration and customer-managed keys.
03:11 - Maya: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, yes. can you share your current KMS provider?
03:20 - Priya Nair: AWS KMS. we also rotate keys quarterly.
03:25 - Maya: fine. we'll include KMS integration checklist.
03:30 - Liam: on SLA targets, can you define minimums? you mentioned p99 target.
03:34 - Roberto: baseline is 99.9% uptime during business hours and p99 latency under 350ms for typical queries; outside business hours we can accept slightly higher latency.
03:46 - Liam: that maps to our Dedicated offering; we can configure autoscaling policies and burst capacity. for hosted we publish historical percentiles but not a dedicated SLO unless on Dedicated/Private.
04:02 - Aisha: what's the fallback behavior if capacity peaks? queueing or degrade to smaller model?
04:08 - Liam: Redwood's smart routing can fall back to cheaper model variants or route to another region based on policy. also we have prefix caching and KV cache to reduce token cost for repeated contexts.
04:26 - Karen: i've seen docs mention KV cache — is that the key-value cache? sometimes transcription says 'K V cash' which confused our devs earlier. :)
04:36 - Maya: yep KV cache, we'll include a brief on how it reduces per-token compute.
04:42 - Aisha: for the pilot, our plan is 3 weeks: week 1 staging and connectivity, week 2 benchmarking and tuning (batching/quant), week 3 evaluate results and cost model.
04:54 - Sofia: sounds good, do we want to lock in dates?
05:00 - Roberto: yes, we want pilot start 4/13 and end 5/1.
05:06 - Maya: we'll schedule the benchmark slot for 4/14. Liam, does that work for your team?
05:11 - Liam: yes 4/14 for the perf run, we'll need sample traces and traffic profile by 4/12.
05:20 - Evan Miller: for traffic profile, we can provide a 48hr trace anonymized, but we need to scrub PII. is that sufficient?
05:28 - Liam: that's ideal. anonymized traces and a few representative prompts. also specify sequence length distribution.
05:36 - Aisha: we will provide that by 4/11.
05:40 - Maya: perfect. switching to security: Priya what are must-haves?
05:45 - Priya: SOC2 / ISO logs, audit trail, SAML/SSO for console, RBAC, and contract requirements for data retention and deletion. also proof of encryption in transit and at rest with customer keys.
06:00 - Maya: Redwood has SOC2 and supports SAML, RBAC and KMS. i'll attach our compliance pack. note on audit logs: we produce detailed request traces and token-level cost breakdowns.
06:18 - Priya: can you provide sample audit log format? some of our auditors expect a certain schema.
06:24 - Maya: we'll include a sample log snippet in the security pack.
06:29 - Roberto: how do you handle data retention for logs? we need 1 year logs for compliance.
06:35 - Maya: default retention is 90 days; enterprise add-on for 12 months available. we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
06:44 - Roberto: good.
06:47 - Aisha: technical deep dive question: what's the recommended quantization level for our models to balance latency vs quality?
06:54 - Liam: depends on model family; for many open models 4-bit quant offers big savings with small quality loss, but we'll run ablations during pilot. we also recommend continuous batching tuned to your request profile.
07:09 - Aisha: great. please include suggestions in perf plan.
07:14 - Maya: on rollouts — after pilot we recommend canary rollouts pinned to model versions and fallback policies. we'll prepare a suggested rollout timeline.
07:25 - Karen: on operational side, we'll need runbooks for incidents and escalation. can you share your oncall playbook?
07:32 - Sofia: yes we have a standard incident playbook and escalation matrix for customers; we'll send it.
07:37 - Aisha: one more on metrics — do you export Prometheus metrics or integrate with our tracing?
07:42 - Liam: we export Prometheus-style metrics and have tracing hooks for Zipkin/OpenTelemetry. we can push to your observability endpoint or you can pull from ours.
07:53 - Evan: we'll prefer pushing to our central OTEL collector. any auth requirements?
07:58 - Maya: we'll include collector config and auth options in the runbook.
08:03 - Roberto: quick question about cost: do you show per-route token-level cost by default?
08:09 - Liam: yes, per-route and per-token cost breakouts available in Redwood Console, and we can provide sample reports.
08:16 - Aisha: great that's what we need for finance signoff.
08:19 - Maya: ok time to recap actions and timeline. we agreed Maya to send staging runbook and security pack by 4/09, Liam to prepare benchmark harness and perf plan by 4/12, SummitCore to provide traces and CIDR by 4/11, and we'll run pilot benchmark on 4/14.
08:40 - Priya: one admin note — procurement will need a draft contract; can you share standard terms?
08:46 - Maya: yes procurement template and SLA one-pager will be attached to the follow-up email.
08:51 - Roberto: any blockers? 
08:53 - Karen: i'll need the exact peering steps and our infra team will want the diagram; otherwise none.
08:59 - Liam: we'll include diagrams and a quick checklist for firewall rules.
09:04 - Aisha: ok thanks everyone, excited to get started.
09:07 - Maya: thanks, we'll send notes and links — action items in the chat.
09:12 - Sofia: i'll schedule the follow-up and send calendar invites for the 4/14 benchmark.
09:18 - Meeting ends

Note: transcription includes occasional mis-heard words and speaker handoffs; timestamps approximate.
